_comment_why: Every version in this repo is hand-pinned with a comment saying how to bump it:
Argo v3.3.14, cert-manager v1.21.1, istio 1.30.3 in four places, istio-csr v0.17.0,
external-secrets 2.9.0, gateway-api v1.6.1, temporal 1.6.0, keycloakx 7.2.3, plus the
tool pins in the CI workflow. Pinning is right — an unpinned platform chart means the
cluster changes when nobody committed anything. But nothing was telling anyone when a
pin went stale or picked up a CVE, so 'bump it' was a thing that happened when someone
remembered. This turns each pin into a PR that CI renders against our own values files.
Grouping is by blast radius, not by ecosystem: the four Istio charts move as one
release train and MUST NOT be split across PRs, while cert-manager and Argo are each
their own decision with their own upgrade note to read.
_comment_commits: semanticCommits is off because this repo's commit messages are the single word
'fixes'. A bot writing 'chore(deps): ...' would be the only thing in the log that
does not look like the rest of it.
_comment_argocd: The ApplicationSet catalogs are the interesting target and Renovate does not parse
them natively: the chart name, its repository and its version are three sibling keys
on a list element, not a Chart.yaml dependency. The custom managers below teach it
that shape. Each regex is anchored on `chart:` + `repoURL:` + `version:` in that
order, which is exactly how every catalog entry is written.

customManagers.description: L1 platform catalog and L2 deps catalog — Helm charts in ApplicationSet list generators
Vendored Gateway API — the `version` on the catalog element, re-vendored with `just vendor-gateway-api`
Argo CD itself — the ARGO_VERSION pin in the bootstrap script
Tool pins inside CI steps that are not actions (kubeconform, kind)

description: THE ISTIO RELEASE TRAIN. base, cni, istiod and ztunnel are one release and the
control plane will not tolerate them at different versions — istiod at 1.31 with
a 1.30 ztunnel is a broken dataplane, not a partial upgrade. One PR, always.
Never automerged and never grouped with anything else: L1/platform/appset.yaml
records that istio-csr sits mid-chain in the mesh's own trust bootstrap, so an
Istio bump is a change to read release notes for, not to rubber-stamp.
cert-manager and istio-csr are coupled the other way round: istio-csr signs every
workload certificate THROUGH cert-manager, so its supported cert-manager range is
the constraint. Grouped so the pair is evaluated together.
Major bumps of anything that owns cluster state get a PR that says so plainly.
For Temporal in particular a major is a schema migration against an external
database this repo does not own — see the manageSchema note in
GitHub Actions are the one place automerge is reasonable: a bad action version
breaks CI loudly and immediately, and cannot reach the cluster. Patch and minor
only — a major is an interface change to read about.

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: A CVE is not a Monday-morning matter.
